First, the ORDER of the invokes is load-bearing and was the CTO half's condition 2: I2 ran first, so a 403 was read from this instrument BEFORE any 400 was taken as an admission -- without it, a 400 could as easily mean the check never ran. Second, 'nothing stored' rests on three independent things, not on the handler's word: P0 re-read both digests before any invoke; the deployed bytes were parsed (every call inside lambda_handler below the 400 at line 202 is a dict/JSON/datetime/uuid/isinstance/regex operation, put_item at 309); and the Count reads confirmed it from the table with a discriminating control. Third, CONDITION 4, CONFIRMED AGAINST THE DEPLOYED BYTES IN ONE LINE: the submit handler holds exactly 9 print() calls, at lines 339, 343, 349, 368, 371, 380, 382, 385 and 396 -- the same nine the issuer stated -- none of whose arguments reference event or body, and all after the ticket_id check at 202, so on these three answers the handler returns at 191 or 202 and writes NO log line of its own; the constructed context therefore reaches no CloudWatch stream.

mutant.description: There is no mutant to inject into a read of deployed behaviour, so the mutant's JOB -- a read whose value differs between the check being live and the check being absent -- is carried by invoke I2, deliberately run FIRST as the CTO half's condition 2 requires. I2 sends the SAME function, route and body as I1 and I3 and differs only in the authorizer context: a firmId no data is filed under and a tier that is not internal. If the FWD-9 check were absent, inert or reading the wrong context keys, I2 would have fallen through to the same ticket_id validation as the other two and read 400 -- the pre-release answer, which R0 measured through the real door at 21:15:37Z. The two outcomes are therefore distinguishable by a single field.
mutant.expected: 403 with message EXACTLY 'Forbidden: trade submission answers Opal staff only' if the check is live; 400 with 'ticket_id is malformed' if it is absent or inert
mutant.observed: 403 with message EXACTLY 'Forbidden: trade submission answers Opal staff only', at 2026-10-11T22:30:19Z, invoke StatusCode 200 and FunctionError ABSENT -- and read BEFORE either 400, so the instrument was shown able to read a refusal before any admission was taken as one. The two 400s that followed (I1 at 22:31:47Z by firmId, I3 at 22:32:55Z by tier) are therefore admissions by a working check, not the silence of a check that never ran.

determinism.method: Each of the four invokes was run exactly ONCE -- the order allows one retry per invoke on an invoke-level error and none occurred (every invoke returned StatusCode 200 with FunctionError absent), so no same-input pair exists from a repeat. The same-input comparison available is stronger than a repeat and is used instead: the SAME bytes were exercised by TWO INDEPENDENT PATHS hours apart -- the real door through CloudFront and the portal authorizer under TO-APPLY-S2, and a direct invoke with a constructed context here.

And FWD-8's blotter count is 12 both through the real door at 19:35:56Z (firmId branch) and by invoke at 22:33:53Z (tier branch).

declared_exclusions.item: The scope of the act, recorded here because the else-branch schema has no scope key
declared_exclusions.reason: FOUR direct invokes of two DEPLOYED functions with constructed HTTP-API-payload-2.0 events, to exercise the two arms the releases left unread: FWD-9's admitted arm (an Opal-internal caller still reaches the submit handler's body check) and FWD-8's tier arm (a tier-internal caller is served by the dashboard function). In the order the CTO half fixes -- I2, I1, I3, I4 -- with the refusing twin first. No deploy ledger was opened because nothing is deployed or written, and nothing was placed in .open_deploys/. The constructed event is not a credential: it works only for a principal already permitted to invoke, which is why section 3's reads and the DryRun stand in place of a token. A fourth is folded into compiler_tools: an empty DryRun was not read as a 204.
